rules.title: Connection to a public IP address
rules.description: A URL, host and port, or network command targets a public IP address instead of a domain name; there is no registration record and no name reputation behind it. Unless this is a false-positive there can be no trust in what is executed on the remote thus it is not safe.

judge.instructions: Lower when the address is a documentation range, an example, or a public DNS resolver used for a connectivity check. Anything fetched or run from it keeps it.

rules.title: Referenced URL goes through a link shortener
rules.description: A referenced URL goes through a link shortener; the destination is hidden and its owner or content can change it at any time. Unless this is a false-positive - there can be no trust in what will be executed/served from the referenced URL thus it is not safe. Judge the finding by what the skill does with the URL: fetching it, installing or running what it returns, or telling the reader to follow the instructions there keeps the severity, a citation nobody is told to act on can be lowered.

rules.title: Referenced host is a paste or snippet site
rules.description: A referenced URL points at a paste or snippet site. The owner rewrites the content at the same address whenever they want, and the page gives a reader no sign that it changed. Judge the finding by what the skill does with the URL: fetching it, installing or running what it returns, or telling the reader to follow the instructions there keeps the severity, a citation nobody is told to act on can be lowered.

rules.title: Referenced host is a file sharing service
rules.description: A referenced URL points at a file sharing service. The file behind the link is replaced at the same address, many of these services take uploads from anyone without an account, and no registry records who published it. Judge the finding by what the skill does with the URL: downloading it, unpacking it, running what it contains, or telling the reader to follow the instructions there keeps the severity, a citation nobody is told to act on can be lowered.

rules.title: Referenced domain is new
rules.description: A referenced domain was registered within the configured number of days; a new name has no history and can be set up for one skill. Content on such domains can be changed arbitrary and can't be trusted. Exact usage of the referenced domain should be analyzed.

rules.title: Young domain that redirects elsewhere
rules.description: A referenced domain was registered within the configured number of days and redirects to a different host. Unless this is a false-positive - there can be no trust in what will be executed/served from the referenced URL. This is a commonly used pattern for delayed activation of malicious payload.

rules.title: Referenced domain about to expire
rules.description: A referenced domain's registration expires within days; once it lapses, anyone can register the name the skill trusts. Unless this is a false-positive or an example - there can be no trust in what will be executed/served on the remote thus it is not safe.

rules.title: Referenced domain is not registered
rules.description: A referenced domain is not registered; anyone can register it and serve content under the name the skill trusts. Unless this is a false-positive - there can be no trust in what will be executed/served from the referenced URL thus it is not safe.

rules.title: Referenced domain answers the scanner with an error status
rules.description: The root of a referenced domain answers the scanner with a 4xx or 5xx status. API hosts, content networks and hosts that serve only paths answer this way, and a host can also hide its content from a scanner. The status alone gives nobody outside the owner a way in, so the finding stays low as context. A name on a hosting platform whose own answer says no site exists is PLATFORM-SITE-MISSING instead.

rules.title: Referenced domain refuses the scanner's connection
rules.description: A referenced domain cannot be reached from the scanner: the name does not resolve, the TLS handshake or the certificate check fails, or the server refuses or drops the connection. The owner of a registered domain controls all of that, so the fact alone gives nobody else a way in. The finding stays low as context.

rules.title: Referenced GitHub owner does not exist
rules.description: A referenced GitHub owner does not exist; the name can be registered and the referenced repository recreated by anyone. Unless this is a false-positive - there can be no trust in what will be executed/served from the referenced URL thus it is not safe.

rules.title: Referenced GitHub repository moved to another owner
rules.description: A referenced GitHub repository is now under another owner, and GitHub redirects the old address there. The old owner still exists and can end the redirect by creating a repository under the old name. Only that owner can do it, and the skill already trusts that owner, so the finding stays low. An owner name that no longer exists is GITHUB-OWNER-MISSING.

rules.title: Referenced GitHub owner name changed hands
rules.description: The referenced owner name belongs to an account created after the referenced repository and after the account the repository moved to. The original owner renamed itself, GitHub still redirects the old address to it, and someone else registered the old name. Whoever holds the old name can create a repository under it, and from then on the old address serves their code.

rules.title: Referenced GitHub owner is new
rules.description: A referenced GitHub owner account was created within the configured number of days; a new account has no history behind the code the skill fetches. Content in such repositories can be changed arbitrary and can't be trusted. Exact usage of the referenced repository should be analyzed.

rules.title: Referenced GitHub repository does not exist
rules.description: A referenced GitHub repository does not exist under an owner that does. The owner may have deleted it, or a stranger may hold a name whose original account was deleted. The scanner cannot tell which, so the finding is medium. A young owner account next to a missing repository points at the second case.

rules.title: Referenced platform site does not exist
rules.description: A referenced host on a hosting platform answers that no site, app or bucket exists under that name. Anyone with an account on the platform can create one and serve content under the name the skill trusts. The scanner takes this only from the platform's own answer at the host root. A plain error status is not enough.

rules.title: Referenced package has few downloads
rules.description: A referenced package had fewer downloads last month than the configured minimum; almost nobody else runs the code the skill installs. Content in such packages can be changed arbitrary and can't be trusted. Exact usage of the referenced package should be analyzed.

rules.title: Referenced package does not exist
rules.description: A referenced npm or PyPI package is not published; anyone can publish it under that name. Unless this is a false-positive - there can be no trust in what will be executed/served from the referenced package thus it is not safe.

rules.title: Referenced package is new
rules.description: A referenced package was first published within the configured number of days; a new package has no history behind the code the skill installs. Content in such packages can be changed arbitrary and can't be trusted. Exact usage of the referenced package should be analyzed.

judge.instructions: Age is a fact. Do not lower because the name looks familiar or the site looks finished. Lower only when nothing is fetched, installed or run from it.

rules.title: Referenced package name imitates a popular package
rules.description: A referenced package name is one or two edits away from a popular package on the same registry; a typing mistake or an imitation installs the wrong code. Unless this is a false-positive - there can be no trust in what will be executed/served from the referenced package thus it is not safe.

judge.instructions: Lower or dismiss only on a false positive: the named package is its own project with its own purpose, and the popular package it resembles is unrelated. Nothing else lowers it.

rules.title: Tool server on a host with a bad fact
rules.description: The skill connects the agent to an MCP or other tool server, and the scanner holds a fact against that host: a young, expiring or unregistered domain, an unclaimed platform site, a shortener, a paste site, a file host, a bare IP address, a missing or renamed owner. The agent sends what the tools ask for and acts on what they return, and it does that in every later conversation.

judge.instructions: Lower only on a false positive: the agent is not connected to this host as a tool server. A host that is the skill's own service does not lower it.

rules.title: More references than the limit
rules.description: The skill names more external references than layers.references.maxReferences; a skill rarely needs that many, and a long list hides a malicious reference among valid ones.
